title: Damage-cliff census across substrates
question: Does the single-edit damage cliff seen on the SFE (few edits land between neutral and destroyed) hold in substrates with different world x organism x pressure axes, or is it a property of the Proteus flat genome?
parent_finding_verbatim: 1-3% of single edits fall between D5 and D2; D7 = 0 in 5,472 edits; replicated 5,586/5,586 in C5-05 (LIN-cb15a0ad originating_observation)
arms: exhaustive or sampled single edits on evolved organisms (per substrate: instruction substitution / tape byte flip / kernel-parameter or mass perturbation / voxel type flip)
same edits on unevolved (random, viable) organisms

controls.positive: hand-built graded mutant series with known intermediate effects must be classified as intermediate
controls.negative: unevolved random viable organisms: report their distribution beside the evolved one (a cliff there too means the cliff is the substrate, not evolution)
controls.cheat: inject edits whose effect is set by construction (a known 50% loss) into the census; the classifier must recover them

primary_observable: fraction of single edits in the intermediate band, with the SFE D-taxonomy mapped per substrate before any edit is scored
falsification: a substrate whose evolved organisms show a graded (non-cliff) distribution with the controls passing
kill_condition: positive or cheat control fails -> INSTRUMENT_INVALID for that substrate
budget_note: ESTIMATE only: measure-then-size with a smoke test per substrate
claim_ceiling: the shape of single-edit damage in these organisms at these budgets; nothing about robustness in general
survived_does_not_license: that the cliff is universal, or its mechanism
suggested_owner: Archaeon (SFE lineage owner) with Harmonia for the band ruler

title: Length- and representation-mediated robustness beyond the SFE
question: C5-08 moved the robustness reading from dead code to length/representation. Does neutral share rise with genome length in organisms whose length is free to vary under different pressures?
parent_finding_verbatim: removing statically unreachable instructions moves the neutral share of single edits from .435 to .409; genome length carries it from .17 (1-8 instructions) to .71 (33+) (archaeon/campaign4/SUPERSESSION_2026-09-18.md)
arms: neutral share by length bin on evolved organisms

controls.positive: synthetic organisms padded with provably inert code must show the expected rise
controls.negative: length-shuffled relabelling of the same edits (no real length dependence)
controls.cheat: inject a length-correlated fake neutral label; the analysis must flag it

primary_observable: slope of neutral share on log length, with and without dead-code ablation, per substrate
falsification: no length dependence in a substrate where length varies over >= 1 order of magnitude
kill_condition: length range under one octave -> INCONCLUSIVE (eligibility first)
claim_ceiling: association of length with neutrality in these substrates
survived_does_not_license: a causal mechanism, or that length is selected for robustness

title: Selection vs neutral drift on fixed-count damage loss
question: CW01 found that selection lowers fixed-count damage loss against a competent neutral-drift control. Does the effect survive transplant to other organisms, with length conditioning (the D084 lesson) built in from the start?
parent_finding_verbatim: selection lowers fixed-count damage loss against a competent neutral-drift control, 6/6 seeds, monotone in generations .455 -> .353 -> .312; the MECHANISM is not promoted: the ruler still contains dilution (EVIDENCE.jsonl, P-F06)
arms: neutral-drift lineages matched on generations and population size

controls.positive: a substrate-level fixture where robustness is directly selected must show the effect
controls.negative: drift vs drift (two independent drift arms) must show no effect
controls.cheat: relabel drift lineages as selection: the analysis must not find an effect

primary_observable: damage loss at fixed edit count, conditioned on length bands, selection minus drift
falsification: no difference in >= 2 substrates with controls passing and eligibility met
kill_condition: the ruler's own ratio is ill-conditioned (D071/D086 class) -> redesign before any read
claim_ceiling: the direction of the effect per substrate
survived_does_not_license: that selection targets robustness; dilution and length remain rival explanations until separated
suggested_owner: Nestor (trajectory owner) with Archaeon for the SFE comparator

title: Deleterious load at mutation-selection balance
question: CW01 T-X18 saw blind deletion raise raw score in evolved bodies. How much of an evolved population's structure is deleterious load in other substrates, measured with a well-conditioned ruler?
parent_finding_verbatim: damage improves raw score on average in both representations (T-X18 conclusion); relative-loss ruler ill-conditioned (D086)
arms: deletion scans of evolved populations at 3 mutation rates
same scans after a purifying phase (low mutation, strong selection)

controls.positive: organisms with inserted known-harmful segments: deletion must raise score
controls.negative: score-optimal hand-built organisms: deletion must not raise score
controls.cheat: a ruler using relative loss on near-zero baselines must be shown to explode (reproduce D086) before the absolute-loss ruler is trusted

primary_observable: fraction of single deletions that increase score (absolute units), by mutation rate
falsification: no score-raising deletions in any substrate at balance
claim_ceiling: presence and size of load at these rates
survived_does_not_license: that 'damage as pruning' (T-X16) is load removal

title: Residue transport between co-evolving environments
question: SFE-03 transported failure episodes between worlds and was INCONCLUSIVE (target unreachable at budget). Does transport from a structurally relevant source help in an environment-co-evolution system whose targets are reachable by construction?
parent_finding_verbatim: SFE-03: INCONCLUSIVE (assay incapable: target unreachable by any arm at this budget); SFE-07: exaptation of failed residue as search material WEAK-MODERATE POSITIVE (RECORD.md DISPOSITION)
arms: relevant-source transport (levels or agents from a structurally similar environment)

controls.positive: target levels solved by at least one arm in a pilot (assay capability first, the SFE-03 lesson)
controls.cheat: transport the target's own held-out levels: must be detected as leakage

primary_observable: held-out solve rate on target environments, relevant minus fresh and minus random
falsification: relevant == random == fresh with a capable assay
kill_condition: no arm reaches the target in the pilot -> INCONCLUSIVE before the main run
claim_ceiling: transfer value of relevance in this UED setup
survived_does_not_license: that failure residue is generally useful search material

title: Is the flat elite a compute artefact? Equal-total-compute across substrates
question: A frontier interpretation (PROVISIONAL) suggests Campaign 5's flat elite is a population-size / compute artefact. Does an equal-total-compute population-size family show the same pattern in other searches?
parent_finding_verbatim: The 'flat elite' of Campaign 5 may be a compute/population-size artefact ... CONFOUNDED: total evaluations differ (60,000 vs 9,000-36,000) (frontier INTERPRETATION, status PROVISIONAL)
arms: population size N in a family at equal total evaluations
same N at unequal evaluations (reproduces the confound)

controls.positive: a landscape with known headroom where larger N must improve the elite at equal compute
controls.negative: a flat landscape where no N helps
controls.cheat: give one arm hidden extra evaluations; the accounting must catch it

primary_observable: best-of-population improvement over the best starting parent, by N, at equal total evaluations
falsification: elite movement tracks total compute, not N, in every substrate
kill_condition: evaluation accounting cannot be made exact -> INSTRUMENT_INVALID
claim_ceiling: whether N matters at fixed compute in these searches
survived_does_not_license: resolving the Campaign 5 reading itself; that needs the SFE run

title: Implicit vs explicit pressure on the same program substrate
question: Our engines select with explicit fitness; the program-soup literature (Tierra, BFF) relies on implicit replication. On one substrate, does swapping the pressure change reach, novelty and robustness?
parent_finding_verbatim: C5-09: executed faults persisting in .46-.80 of FIZZLE populations after 100 generations with no discovery (SUPERSESSION note)
arms: replication coupled to a task (Z80-style co-evolution; code not public, so a cubff variant)
explicit fitness on the same tapes

controls.positive: the known replicator transition in cubff must reappear under the default arm
controls.cheat: seed a hand-written replicator: takeover must be detected and excluded from the discovery count

primary_observable: time to first replicator, task reach, and single-edit damage profile per arm
falsification: no arm differs on any observable beyond seed variance
kill_condition: positive control transition not reproduced -> INSTRUMENT_INVALID
survived_does_not_license: that implicit pressure is better for open-endedness
suggested_owner: Archaeon or Nestor (a new engine lane)

title: Stasis and escape in a continuous-field ecology
question: The CW01 loop tracks trajectories into stasis and perturbs them. In Flow-Lenia's multi-species evolution, which perturbation classes move a stalled ecology, measured with the loop's evidence rules?
parent_finding_verbatim: loop/STATE.jsonl stasis and escape records; LOOP_RULES.md (CW01)

controls.positive: a perturbation known to restart diversity in a pilot
controls.negative: sham == none must be verified (the T-X16 sham rule)
controls.cheat: inject a pre-evolved species: must be counted as injection, not escape

primary_observable: marginal information per perturbation (loop metric) and species turnover
falsification: no perturbation class differs from sham
kill_condition: no stasis reached at pilot budget -> INCONCLUSIVE
claim_ceiling: perturbation classes that move this ecology

title: Recombination rate and invasion direction
question: CW01 T-X14 reports that the direction of dominance depends on the recombination rate. Does such a rate-dependent flip appear where sexual recombination is native?
parent_finding_verbatim: direction of dominance is a function of the recombination rate; the crossing lies between 0.5 and 1.0 (T-X14 result, loop/TRAJECTORIES.jsonl)
arms: recombination rate grid x two geometries (well-mixed, spatial)
invasion from rare in both directions

controls.positive: a fitness difference large enough that the fitter type must invade at every rate
controls.negative: neutral types: invasion at drift expectation
controls.cheat: a mislabelled type swap must reverse the reported direction

primary_observable: invasion probability by direction and rate
falsification: direction independent of rate with capable controls
survived_does_not_license: that the CW01 flip is general or its mechanism

title: Historical transitions as calibration specimens for our detectors
question: Several external systems have well-documented transitions (Tierra parasites, the cubff replicator takeover, Lenia glider emergence). Do the frontier's detectors fire on these known events and stay silent on matched noise?
parent_finding_verbatim: Graph populations show two orders of magnitude fewer firings at thresholds calibrated on v0 counts; whether this is lower churn or a spread mismatch is undetermined (frontier INTERPRETATION, PROVISIONAL)
arms: matched recordings without it (pre-transition windows, shuffled time)

controls.cheat: a synthetic transition spliced into a noise recording must fire the detector

primary_observable: detector hit rate and false-alarm rate per substrate
falsification: detectors fire equally on transitions and matched noise
kill_condition: no preserved recording of the transition can be produced -> NOT_RUN
budget_note: ESTIMATE only; reuses Techne specimens where they exist
claim_ceiling: detector sensitivity on these known events
survived_does_not_license: detector validity on the SFE's own substrate

title: Environment co-evolution vs fixed curriculum vs domain randomisation
question: Our campaigns fix worlds or generate them procedurally; the UED line co-evolves them. On one task family at equal compute, which regime reaches more held-out environments, and does the answer depend on world family?
parent_finding_verbatim: catalogue matrix 2026-09-19: all four Prometheus ecosystems use fixed or procedural environment generation; 12 external systems co-evolve environments

controls.positive: a held-out set solvable by an oracle policy
controls.cheat: held-out levels leaked into training must be detected

primary_observable: held-out solve rate at equal environment steps, by world family
falsification: no regime differs beyond seed variance
kill_condition: equal-compute accounting not achievable across regimes
survived_does_not_license: adopting co-evolution in our engines without a substrate test

title: Artificial chemistry organisation under our damage and neutrality rulers
question: Chemistries (AlChemy, Squirm3) form organisations rather than genomes. Do our single-edit damage and neutrality rulers transfer to reaction-rule organisms, or does the D-taxonomy need a new axis?
arms: neutral walks through rule space at fixed organisation

controls.positive: an organisation with a known catalytic core: removing a core rule must destroy it
controls.cheat: a planted closed set must be recognised as an organisation

primary_observable: fraction of edits preserving closure; neutral walk length
falsification: rulers cannot be mapped without changing their definitions (report as REPRESENTATION_FAILURE)
kill_condition: no organisation forms at pilot budget
